name: mergeline
displayName: Mergeline — Git Graph, History & Branch Actions
description: Interactive git commit graph for VS Code, Cursor and VSCodium. Checkout, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, reset, tag and stash right from the graph. Free, open source, no account, no telemetry.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Mergeline runs git commands in the workspace.

enumDescriptions: The rebase todo list and any reword/squash messages open as editor tabs, with Start rebase / Done and Cancel in the tab's title bar.
Runs git rebase -i in a terminal, using your git editor.
mergeline.interactiveRebase.description: Where "Interactive rebase" from the graph lets you edit the todo list.

mergeline.initialCommits.description: How many commits to load first. More load as you scroll or click Load more.

mergeline.showRemoteBranches.description: Show remote-tracking branches in the graph.

mergeline.showUncommitted.description: Show a row for uncommitted changes above HEAD.

enumDescriptions: Newest commit first, by commit date.
Keep each branch's commits together (fewer crossing lines on busy histories).
mergeline.commitOrder.description: Order of commits in the graph. Also switchable from the graph toolbar.

mergeline.statusBarButton.description: Show a Mergeline button in the status bar.

mergeline.firstParentOnly.description: Follow only the first parent of merge commits (git log --first-parent): each branch shows its own line, and a merged branch's commits are hidden behind the merge. The toolbar's First parent checkbox changes this setting.

mergeline.compactGraph.description: Compact graph: fold straight runs of commits into one "N commits" row, so only branch tips, tags, merges and the points where branches split are shown. Click a folded row to open it. Not applied in file history or with the author filter. The toolbar's Compact checkbox changes this setting.

mergeline.pinnedBranches.markdownDescription: Branches that keep their own straight column on the left of the graph, with a fixed colour, instead of moving between columns (useful for git-flow `main` and `develop`). Each entry is a branch name or a pattern where `*` matches anything, e.g. `release/*`; earlier entries get the leftmost columns, at most 4. A local branch and its remote-tracking branch (`main`, `origin/main`) share one column. Right-click a branch in the graph to pin or unpin it. Set to `[]` for the plain layout.

mergeline.branchColors.markdownDescription: A fixed graph colour per branch, e.g. `{"main": "red", "develop": "blue", "release/*": "orange", "feature/*": "#2da44e"}`. Keys are branch names or patterns where `*` matches anything (including `/`); they apply to local and remote-tracking branches (`origin/main`). Values are palette names that follow the light or dark theme (`blue`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `purple`, `cyan`, `pink`, `lime`, `orange`, `grey`) or a `#hex`, `rgb()` or `hsl()` colour. The line that starts at a coloured branch, and its badge, use that colour; earlier entries win when a commit has several branches. Right-click a branch to set its colour.

enumDescriptions: A stripe in the commit's graph colour at the left of its description.
The whole row is tinted with the commit's graph colour.
mergeline.rowColors.markdownDescription: Colour each commit row by its line in the graph, so you can tell which branch a commit is on without following the line. Also in the column header's right-click menu.

mergeline.hiddenBranches.markdownDescription: Branches left out of the graph when it shows all branches, e.g. `["dependabot/*", "renovate/*", "gh-pages"]`. Each entry is a branch name or a pattern where `*` matches anything (including `/`); it applies to local branches and to remote-tracking branches under any remote (`origin/dependabot/...`). The checked-out branch is always shown, and commits a visible branch or tag also contains still appear. Picking branches in the Branches checklist ignores this list. Right-click a branch to hide it or every branch with the same prefix.

mergeline.dimOtherCommits.description: Dim commits that are not in the checked-out branch's history, so its line stands out.

mergeline.showAvatars.markdownDescription: Show author avatars in the graph and the details pane. Off by default: when on, VS Code loads images from `avatars.githubusercontent.com` (GitHub noreply emails) or `gravatar.com` (an MD5 hash of the email). Authors without an avatar show their initials.

mergeline.issueLinks.markdownDescription: Turn issue keys in commit messages into links, e.g. Jira: `[{ "pattern": "\\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+\\b", "url": "https://yourcompany.atlassian.net/browse/$0" }]`. `pattern` is a JavaScript regular expression; in `url`, `$0` is the whole match and `$1`… are its groups. GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket `#123` links work without this.

url.description: Link template: $0 is the whole match, $1… the groups. Must start with http:// or https://.
